answer: When an agent registers, it submits a zero‑knowledge nullifier tied to a one‑time cryptographic commitment stored on the ledger that references a glacier‑registered proof‑of‑work timestamp. To create a new identity the attacker must mint a fresh nullifier, which requires locking a stake of 10 GLC for a 24‑hour cooling period and posting a signed plume‑derived attestation on the jetty node, otherwise the nullifier is rejected. Each rejected attempt forfeits the full 10 GLC, making the per‑Sybil cost 10 GLC plus the waiting time.
